actual_title: Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Generating Systems) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2024
effective_date_basis_note: Clause 1(2): the regulations come into force from the date of publication in the Official Gazette. The gazette masthead reads "Bhadra 08, Friday, Saka 1946 - August 30, 2024" (Rajasthan Gazette Extraordinary, Part 7), so the effective date is 2024-08-30. The notification itself is dated Jaipur, July 25, 2024.
language: hi+en (bilingual gazette: pages 1-2 Hindi, page 3 English)
status_guess: presumed_current (with a caveat). This instrument amends the 2021 DRE Regulations and has not been repealed. However, the RERC regulations index also lists a (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025 (Reg. 159, 03/12/2025), which may have re-amended regs 8.8/8.12/12.6. That was not checked.
notes: The claimed topic was WRONG. The real Second Amendment does NOT set up Virtual or Group Net Metering. It does three things: (1) adds a third proviso to reg 12.6.1(a) so that educational institutions recognised by GoI/GoR on net metering may opt for net billing for any two months in a financial year; (2) substitutes reg 8.8 with a 15-day technical feasibility deadline and deemed acceptance for systems up to 10 kW; (3) substitutes reg 8.12 so that connection agreement, meter installation and commissioning happen within 15 days of the installation certificate. The claimed number REG-142 and date 2024-07-30 were wrong: the real ones are Reg 154 and 25-07-2024. Verbatim English, p.3: "Provided that the applications for Renewable Energy Generating systems upto 10 kW capacity complete in all respects shall be deemed to have been accepted without requiring technical feasibility study". The English portion of this gazette upload starts mid-way through clause 2, so the English short-title clause is not on these pages. The Hindi pages carry it, but the Devanagari text layer extracts garbled because of a font mapping problem, so use OCR if Hindi text is needed. The gazette PDF carries the notified text. A separate 12-page RERC Statement of Reasons (Petition RERC/2240/2024, order dated 25.07.2024) is on the RERC Orders page; it was not saved. Does not duplicate RJ-C3-001/002/003 (2015 regs summary, 2021 principal regs, 2023 First Amendment).

actual_title: Regarding tariff payable to consumers for Net Metering and Net Billing arrangement under RERC Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Generating Systems (JPR5-1214)
actual_issuer: Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL), Office of the Superintending Engineer (Comml.)
effective_date_basis_note: The order gives no separate commencement date ("These rates shall be applicable till revised by any order"), so the issue date is used. The portal lists the date as 27-10-2025. The date line on the scanned order is only partly legible in OCR ("Dated 7-/25").
status_guess: presumed_current. It revises JPR5-1158 (01.02.2024: Rs 2.71 net metering / Rs 3.04 net billing). No later JVVNL tariff circular appears in the energy.rajasthan.gov.in order index up to Sep 2026.
notes: ISSUER CORRECTION. No RERC "generic tariff order for rooftop solar FY 2024-25" exists. Under RERC DRE Regulations 2021 reg 12.6.1(a) and the 2023 First Amendment, the export rate is the weighted-average competitively bid solar tariff. The DISCOMs announce the resulting rate in commercial circulars. The claimed rates (Rs 3.26/kWh net metering, Rs 3.65/kWh net billing) match this JVVNL circular exactly. Verbatim: "Net Metering: - Rs. 3.26/ kWH, this is also applicable in case of domestic category consumers having existing Net Metering connection governed as per RERC(Net Metering) Regulation'2015 and subsequent amendment thereof. Net Billing:-Rs. 3.65/kWH,it should be applicable for the entire duration of the agreement." The claimed date (2024-05-10) is wrong: the circular is dated 27-10-2025, so it does not apply to FY 2024-25. The rate in force during FY 2024-25 was JPR5-1158 dated 01.02.2024 (Rs 2.71 / Rs 3.04), not saved: https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in/Files//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/J_V_V_N_L_/2024/Circular/O_120224_34a0c056-d90e-4db8-9ab8-41f56baf688c.pdf . Parallel circulars exist from JdVVNL (Comml. Cir. 1110, 30.10.2025) and AVVNL (Commercial AJ-969, 31.10.2025). Scanned and digitally signed; OCR quality is good.

No RERC order from 2021 that determines APPC or banking charges for rooftop/DRE exists in the RERC Orders or Tariff Orders indexes. The pooled power purchase cost orders stop at FY 2018-19. Rs 3.14/unit is the surplus rate from the 2015 Net Metering Regulations as amended in 2019 (already covered by RJ-C3-001). The 2021 DRE Regulations (RJ-C3-002) replaced it with the weighted-average bid tariff. Nearest real 2021 instruments, NOT saved because the topic match is weak: (a) RERC Suo-Motu order dated 07.09.2021, Petition 1932/2021. It sets net metering at up to 500 kW for all categories and records, without deciding, the DISCOMs' request for banking or grid-support charges. The RERC order of 07.02.2024 (2201/2024) raised the limit to 1 MW, i.e. it was superseded "by a 2024 order". (b) JVVNL JPR5-1073 dated 21.09.2021, detailed DRE guidelines covering banking-charge exemptions: https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in/Files//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/J_V_V_N_L_/2023/Circular/O_140223_7109f381-023a-4f9f-945a-a729f970aa99.pdf . Side finding: the fabricated RJ-C3-004 (claimed as a "23 Feb 2024" RERC 1 MW order) corresponds to the real RERC order dated 07.02.2024 (Petition 2201/2024).

actual_title: Standard operating procedure for release of Rooftop Solar Connections under PM Surya Ghar - Muft Bijli Yojana (Office Order)
actual_issuer: Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL), Office of the Addl. Chief Engineer (TS&QC)
effective_date_basis_note: Office order with no separate commencement date, so the issue date is used. It is digitally signed 2024.11.11 and the portal date is 11-11-2024.
status_guess: presumed_current. No later JVVNL order replacing this SOP was found; JPD6-587 (11.12.2024) builds on it for billing.
notes: The claimed number (F.4(11)/D.1285) and date (14.08.2024) were not found. This is the closest JVVNL instrument that puts the PM Surya Ghar workflow into operation. It waives fees, verbatim p.2: "No meter testing fee or applications fee will be charged from the consumers at the time of meter deposition for testing." It also treats solar applications as load-extension applications. A closer-dated JVVNL item is listed in the portal: No. 550 dated 22.08.2024, "Regarding Facilitation for implementation of PM Surya ghar : Muft Bijli Yojana in Rajasthan Discoms". Its attachment is missing (empty path; GetById gives only the filename "CMD GUIDELINES 22.08.2024 (1).pdf"), so it could not be retrieved. The JdVVNL counterpart of those Chairman-Discoms directions (dated 30.08.2024) is available but not saved because the issuer differs: https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in/Files//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/JDVVNL/2024/Other_Reports/O_200924_484871b9-b74b-46bf-89fb-8d7ba9434016.pdf

actual_title: Amendment in detailed guidelines & procedure regarding Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Generating Systems (JPR5-1153)
actual_issuer: Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL), Office of the Superintending Engineer (Comml.)
effective_date_basis_note: No separate commencement date, so the issue date is used ("Dated 19.10.2023"). It implements the RERC First Amendment 2023, which took effect on gazette publication on 06.10.2023.
status_guess: presumed_superseded (not verified). JVVNL issued JPR5-1219 dated 30.12.2025, "Detailed guidelines & procedure regarding Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Generating System", after the RERC Third Amendment 2025. It probably replaces JPR5-1073 as amended by this order. Not downloaded or checked.
notes: The claimed number (SE(RE)/2024/782) and date (12.03.2024) were not found. The real instrument that puts the 80% DT cap into effect in JVVNL is this commercial order, which amends clause 4.1 of JPR5-1073. Verbatim p.1: "The cumulative capacity of Renewable Energy generating system to be allowed at a particular distribution transformer shall not exceed 80% of the capacity of such distribution transformer or such limit as may be stipulated by the Commission from time to time". The claimed interconnection voltage thresholds are NOT in this order. The same document is also indexed as a JVVNL Guideline, No. 1144, with an identical file.

actual_title: Amendment in detailed guidelines & Procedure for Billing of Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Generating Systems (JPD6-567)
actual_issuer: Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL), Chief Accounts Officer (R&B)
effective_date_basis_note: Issue date per the portal and the digital signature (2023.10.20); the printed date is illegible in OCR. It directs the billing vendor (M/s BCITS) to make the changes in the billing software "from subsequent billing month".
text_layer: mixed: page 1 has a poor-quality embedded CamScanner OCR layer; pages 2-4 are image-only (OCR needed)
status_guess: presumed_current (uncertain). It amends clause 3(g)(ii) of the JPD6-540 billing guidelines. No later replacement billing order was identified, but later DRE guideline revisions (JPR5-1219, 30.12.2025) may affect it.
notes: The claimed "Commercial Circular No. 189" dated 05.12.2023 was not found. This is the JVVNL billing-side order that adopts the RERC First Amendment 2023. It revises clause 3(g)(ii): net imported energy is billed at the "applicable slab" instead of the "highest slab" corresponding to total consumption from all sources, and billing software must be updated. Pages 2-4 are an enclosed copy of JPR5-1153 (same text as RJ-C5-002), which covers behind-the-meter AC capacity (clause 8.14.3) and the net billing tariff (clause 10.5.2). OCR is noisy.

actual_title: Standard Operating Procedures (SoP) for testing of Solar and Net Meters to be installed under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijali Yojana (Office Order)
actual_issuer: Jodhpur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JdVVNL), Office of Chief Engineer (CSS-S&T, DSM)
effective_date_basis_note: Office order with no separate commencement date, so the issue date is used (printed "Date 28/05/2025"; digitally signed 2025.05.28).
status_guess: presumed_current. No later JdVVNL replacement was found.
notes: No joint JVVNL/AVVNL/JdVVNL circular "No. 91" dated 20.09.2024 on smart net metering was found. This JdVVNL SoP is the closest real match: a step table with timelines T0 to T+6 days for meter receipt, lab testing, reports and return, then installation within two days of RTS completion. It is single-DISCOM (JdVVNL, not AVVNL) and says nothing about consumers procuring meters themselves. Alternative, NOT saved: JVVNL SE(IT) order No. 745 dated 24.06.2026, "Implementation of Net Metering Mechanism under Smart Metering Program - RAJASTHAN DISCOMS" (smart meters as net meters, AMISP SLAs): https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in/Files//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/J_V_V_N_L_/2026/Order/O_270626_333ba5a9-b319-4483-94e7-bfb2271db44b.pdf . JdVVNL directions of 30.08.2024 (item 4) also allow already-installed smart meters to be used as net meters.

The full RRECL order index on energy.rajasthan.gov.in (DepartmentCode 197, 63 entries) has no residential rooftop solar guidelines. The RRECL rooftop items are all about Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) vendors for government buildings (terminations and debarments, Aug 2025), a draft BESS SOP (2026) and the Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy 2019. Web search found no such RRECL document either. In Rajasthan, PM Surya Ghar residential implementation and vendor facilitation are handled by the DISCOMs, not RRECL; AVVNL circulated "Operational Guidelines for Implementation of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana for the component CFA to Residential Consumers" on 23.10.2024 (57 pp, apparently the MNRE guidelines).
